مُقْرُوحٌ : see قَرِيحٌ. ―
-b2- Also Having قُرُوح [or purulent pustules]. (K.) ―
-b3- Also A young weaned camel attacked by the disease termed قُرْح; [see قَرْحٌ;] as also ↓ قَارِحٌ : or a camel attacked by the disease termed قُرْحَة; as also ↓ قَرِيحٌ and ↓ مُقَرَّحٌ : (L:) one says ↓ إِبِلٌ مُقَرَّحَةٌ , [accord. to some copies of the K مُقَرِّحَةٌ, but erroneously, for it is from قُرِّحَ,] meaning camels having قُرُوح [or purulent pustules] in their mouths, in consequence of which their lips hang down; (K;) and so إِبِلٌ قَرْحَى [in which the epithet is pl. of ↓ قَرِيحٌ ]. (L.) ―
-b4- And طَرِيقٌ مَقْرُوحٌ (assumed tropical:) A road in which marks, or tracks, have been made [by the feet of men and of beasts], so that it has been rendered conspicuous. (K, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
